nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group, let $F_n$ be the free group on the basis $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, and let $T \subseteq F_n$. The $G$-closure $\mathrm{cl}_G(T)$ is the set of $w \in F_n$ such that $\mu(w) = 1$ for every homomorphism $\mu : F_n \to G$ with $\mu(t) = 1$ for all $t \in T$, that is, the intersection of the kernels of all homomorphisms $F_n \to G$ that vanish on $T$.
nodes.title: Closure of a set of words with respect to a group

nodes.summary: Two groups $G$ and $H$ are geometrically equivalent (B. I. Plotkin) when $\mathrm{cl}_G(T) = \mathrm{cl}_H(T)$ for every natural number $n$ and every subset $T$ of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$, where $\mathrm{cl}_G(T)$ is the $G$-closure of $T$: the intersection of the kernels of all homomorphisms $F_n \to G$ that vanish on $T$.
nodes.title: Geometrically equivalent groups

nodes.summary: Let $q$ be a quasi-identity with unknowns $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, premises $w_1, \dots, w_k$ and conclusion $w$, all in the free group $F_n$ on $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. For $g_0, \dots, g_{n-1}$ in a group $G$ and $u \in F_n$, write $u(g_0, \dots, g_{n-1})$ for the image of $u$ under the homomorphism $F_n \to G$ sending each $x_j$ to $g_j$. nodes.title: Satisfaction of a quasi-identity in a group

nodes.summary: A quasi-identity consists of a natural number $n$, a finite list of premises $w_1, \dots, w_k$ and a conclusion $w$, all elements of the free group $F_n$ on the unknowns $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. It stands for the formula $\forall x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}\, (w_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_k = 1 \to w = 1)$.
nodes.title: Quasi-identities of groups

nodes.summary: The statement of Kourovka Problem 14.71 is false: there are groups $G$ and $H$ such that every quasi-identity holds in $G$ if and only if it holds in $H$, but $G$ and $H$ are not geometrically equivalent.
nodes.title: Groups with the same quasi-identities need not be geometrically equivalent

nodes.summary: The proposition (Kourovka Problem 14.71, B. I. Plotkin) that any two groups $G$ and $H$ satisfying the same quasi-identities, meaning that every quasi-identity holds in $G$ if and only if it holds in $H$, are geometrically equivalent.
nodes.title: Plotkin's problem on quasi-identities and geometric equivalence

can_prove.label: ready to prove

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.
